reason: Only Chromium aborts a request with a reason (interception.abortReason); Firefox and WebKit report one failure for every reason, so Route.abort("internetDisconnected") there is refused and the request continues

route.fallback({ url }) hands the request to the next matching route with a new URL, and chains through three routes; Route.continueWith can change the URL (interception.continueUrl) but never passes the request on to the next route

The original calls route.continue() after the frame was removed and checks that the call doesn't throw; a Strider handler returns its decision, which is applied after the handler returns, and a decision that can't be applied is logged, not raised to the handler
Playwright's it.skip runs this only on WebKit, and it tests the exception route.fulfill throws for a redirect status, which only Playwright's WebKit refuses
Strider doesn't refuse a fulfilled redirect status: the handler returns its fulfilled response as a decision, so there is no call that throws the refusal
A route registered with times removes itself after that many requests; Strider's routes have no times option, and a route stays until its registration is removed

The original calls route.fulfill, route.continue, route.fallback, and route.abort a second time and checks that the second call throws "Route is already handled!"; a Strider handler produces one decision, so there is no second call to make
A URLPattern with ignoreCase: Strider's URL patterns are strings, and a URLPattern string has no case-insensitive option
